artists.biography:
Cake is an American alternative rock band from Sacramento, California. Consisting of singer John McCrea, trumpeter Vince DiFiore, guitarist Xan McCurdy, bassist Gabe Nelson and drummer Paulo Baldi, the band has been noted for McCrea's sarcastic lyrics and deadpan voice, DiFiore's trumpet parts, and their wide-ranging musical influences, including country music, Mariachi, rock, funk, Iranian folk music and hip-hop.
Cake was formed in 1991 by McCrea, DiFiore, Greg Brown, Frank French and Shon Meckfessel, who soon left and was replaced by Nelson. Following the self-release of its debut album, Motorcade of Generosity, the band was signed to Capricorn Records in 1995 and released its first single, "Rock 'n' Roll Lifestyle", which hit number 35 on the Modern Rock Tracks music chart and was featured on MTV's 120 Minutes; French and Nelson then left the band, and were replaced by Todd Roper and Victor Damiani. Cake's second album, 1996's Fashion Nugget, went platinum on the strength of its lead single, "The Distance". Following a tour of Europe and the United States, both Brown and Damiani announced they were leaving Cake, which led to speculation about the band's future; McCrea eventually recruited Xan McCurdy to take over on guitar, and persuaded Nelson to return.
Prolonging the Magic, the band's third album, was released in 1998 and went platinum, having shipped over one million units; this was followed three years later by Comfort Eagle, the band's first album on Columbia Records, featuring the single "Short Skirt/Long Jacket" which hit number 7 on the Modern Rock Tracks chart. Following a series of tours, including several versions of the Unlimited Sunshine Tour, the band released Pressure Chief in 2004, its second and last album on Columbia. After creating its own label, Upbeat Records, the band released Showroom of Compassion in 2011, which became its first album to debut at the top of the Billboard charts, selling 44,000 copies in the first week after release.

perplexity.description:
Prolonging the Magic is the third studio album by American alternative rock band Cake, originally released on October 6, 1998, under Capricorn Records (later distributed by Sony Music). The album showcases Cake’s signature blend of alternative pop/rock, post-grunge, and adult alternative, marked by John McCrea’s deadpan vocals, sparse guitar riffs, and the prominent use of trumpet and keyboard. The sound is both minimalist and eclectic, with tracks like “Never There” and “Sheep Go to Heaven” highlighting the band’s knack for catchy hooks and offbeat arrangements. The album was recorded after the departure of guitarist Greg Brown, with a rotating lineup filling in, including Xan McCurdy, who would later become a permanent member.

In Cake’s discography, Prolonging the Magic solidified their reputation for quirky, genre-defying rock and helped expand their mainstream appeal. The album debuted at No. 33 on the Billboard 200 and was certified platinum by the RIAA in 1999 for selling over one million copies. Its lead single, “Never There,” topped the Modern Rock Tracks chart and reached the Top 40 on the Adult Top 40, while “Sheep Go to Heaven” and “Let Me Go” also achieved notable chart success. Critics praised the album for its distinctive style and consistent songwriting, cementing its place as a standout release in Cake’s catalog and a defining work of late-1990s alternative rock.
